summary: Verified conversion-error propagation E2E. Backend flag persistence + sub-recipe bubble-up + UI banner in Recipe Builder all WORK. Found ONE bug: PUT /api/inventory/ingredients/{id} that ONLY changes density_g_per_ml does not trigger the recipe recalc cascade (cascade gate requires cost_changed or waste_changed), so has_conversion_errors stays stale on recipes even after the ingredient's density is populated.

critical.issue: Setting density_g_per_ml on an ingredient does NOT trigger _recalc_recipes_using_ingredient. The cascade condition (routers/inventory.py ~line 413) is `if cost_changed or waste_changed:` — density change is not included. Consequence: a recipe that previously had has_conversion_errors=true because of missing density stays flagged True forever until the recipe is manually re-saved or another cost/waste change on the same ingredient triggers the cascade. This directly breaks the acceptance criterion 'flag flips back to false after density set'. Repro: create ingredient base=kg no density, create recipe with unit=L on that ingredient (flag=true), PUT density_g_per_ml=1.2 on the ingredient → GET recipe still shows has_conversion_errors=true.

issues: Banner text is in English ('Incomplete cost — 1 ingredient with unresolved conversion') even though UI language toggle is Spanish in some places. Not blocking — actual text depends on `language` state; requirement mentioned Spanish 'Costo incompleto — 1 ingrediente...'. In current session the UI happened to be English. The line-level inline warning IS in Spanish ('Sin conversión disponible... missing density_g_per_ml'), which is a mild inconsistency.

action_items: In /app/backend/routers/inventory.py update_ingredient (~line 379-413): also detect density_g_per_ml change and weight_per_unit_g change and include them in the cascade trigger. Something like: density_changed = float(current.get('density_g_per_ml') or 0) != float(new_density or 0); wpu_changed = same for weight_per_unit_g; then `if cost_changed or waste_changed or density_changed or wpu_changed:` call _recalc_recipes_using_ingredient.
Optional: also refresh the recipe when the ingredient's base_unit changes (edge case).
critical_code_review_comments: Cascade trigger in inventory.update_ingredient is too narrow — should include unit-conversion metadata (density_g_per_ml, weight_per_unit_g, base_unit) changes, otherwise the has_conversion_errors flag becomes sticky.
Banner label mixes languages between the inline error and the summary banner — recommend routing both through the same i18n key.

success_rate.backend: 3/4 acceptance criteria pass — density override, initial flag persistence, sub-recipe bubble-up, cost-breakdown fields all work; flag-flip-back-to-false FAILS.

Root cause identified in inventory.update_ingredient cascade gate. Once main agent adds density_changed/wpu_changed to that gate, re-run: `cd /app/backend && pytest tests/test_conversion_error_e2e_api.py -v`.
rca of the issue: In /app/backend/routers/inventory.py update_ingredient the recalc cascade is guarded by `if cost_changed or waste_changed:`. When a user only sets density_g_per_ml (to resolve a conversion error) neither branch is true, so _recalc_recipes_using_ingredient is never called and the recipe's has_conversion_errors, conversion_errors and conversion_errors_count remain stale. Fix: add density_changed and weight_per_unit_g_changed detection and include them in the trigger.
